description: Engineers bridging the physical and digital frontiers.
summary:
Cosmitility is an AI-powered health monitoring software designed to inform and advise astronauts about their well-being throughout their mission, with the main feature being Ms. HOA, which is an AI assistant built to turn health monitoring compact and immersive. By analyzing processed data, collected during the crew's activities, the AI can give immediate yet practical insights along with suggestions. The AI also has an integrated text-to-speech function, thus allowing it to communicate with crewmates on a daily basis and making information more accessible while building a sense of connection in such an isolating environment as space. 
Besides that, the app also provides interactive graphics and visualizations for incoming data, based on the five hazards of space exploration, this feature allows the astronauts to track not just their health but also the entire crew's well-being.
This project aims to turn complex health information into something more comprehensible and convenient to astronauts, helping them understand their overall health and improve the overall efficiency of the expedition to Mars.
details:
Cosmitility is a local AI-powered health monitoring app designed to inform and advise astronauts about their health, the way it works is by converting the processed data into interactive dashboards and illustrations. Additionally, the AI can learn from that data and then alert crewmates about their overall well-being. The software was developed using JavaScript, CSS, and HTML in Visual Studio Code.

The main feature is Ms. HOA, an AI assistant that analyses available health data and provides explanations, observations, and suggestions to the user, it is also very important that we mention Ms.HOA's 2D model is hand-drawn by our team's artist in Krita with 4 expressions, including happy, sad, shocked, and neutral. The project runs the Qwen3.5-4B model locally to generate responses and control the actions of the 2D model. In order to turn text into speech, the Kokoro model is used to allow Ms. HOA to communicate verbally with the astronauts, turning something as boring as reading a bunch of numbers about health metrics into a more fun and engaging experience

To upload the processed data, we developed a function to read CSV file, then what was read is plotted against time on a graph (or update an already existing graph with a new point). In addition, astronauts can modify their own dashboard to choose what information they want to see, which can help astronauts customize and see the more important metrics. It is also possible for the astronauts to monitor both their personal health and the condition of their crewmates in one place, we thought of this feature in case of emergency situations where it's a hassle to find the crewmate's tablet to access their health. And in these situations, this feature also allows them to receive AI-assisted suggestions to recognise potential concerns and make informed decisions.

Our project's creativity shines in the integration of the AI model into the software, rather than functioning as a conventional data dashboard, it gives the astronauts an interactive assistant who can help them understand their own well-being and also maintain awareness over the entire crew.

Throughout the development of this project, we considered the unique challenges of Mars missions, particularly communication delays, isolation, radiation, lack of gravity, accessibility, and the importance of reliable information, which is also why we also prioritized keeping the AI and voice-processing components locally runnable, reducing reliance on continuous internet connectivity.
